title: 2000 AMC 12 Problem 13
statement: One morning each member of Angela’s family drank an \(8\)-ounce mixture of coffee with milk. The amounts of coffee and milk varied from cup to cup, but were never zero. Angela drank a quarter of the total amount of milk and a sixth of the total amount of coffee. How many people are in the family?

solutions.text:
Measure amounts in \(8\)-ounce cups, so Angela’s cup holds \(c\) coffee and \(m\) milk with \(c + m = 1.\)

Since Angela drank a sixth of the coffee, the total coffee is \(6c\); since she drank a quarter of the milk, the total milk is \(4m.\) The number of people equals the total number of cups, \[ \begin{aligned} 6c + 4m &= 6c + 4(1 - c) \\ &= 4 + 2c. \end{aligned} \]

This is an integer only when \(2c\) is an integer, and since \(0 \lt c \lt 1\) this forces \(c = \tfrac12,\) giving \(4 + 1 = 5\) people.

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Suppose Angela’s own cup contains \(c\) units of coffee and \(m\) units of milk with \(c + m = 1\)
Then the family total is \(6c\) coffee and \(4m\) milk, so the number of people is \(6c + 4m\)
